provenance._note: R9700/gfx1201 static hardware constants (cu_count/vgprs_per_simd/max_waves_per_simd/lds_bytes_per_cu/wavefront_size) per docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-01-gfx1201-phaseA-perf-instrument.md Global Constraints. lds_bytes_per_cu=65536 (64 KiB) matches the single source of truth (profiler.rs::arch_spec, used identically for every RDNA1-4 arch incl. gfx1100/gfx1200/gfx1201) and is what ROCm/HIP reports as the per-CU LDS partition; the plan prose's '128KiB' figure is the physical LDS size per WGP (shared by 2 CUs), not per-CU, and committing 131072 here would make verify_live fail loud against every real gfx1201 card. vram_mb=32768 is the R9700 (Radeon AI PRO, 32GB, hiptrx). cu_count=64 confirmed via rocminfo on the live R9700 AND the local RX 9070 XT — both are the full Navi 48 (64 CU); profiler.rs's comment lists 'RX 9070 (56 CU) / RX 9070 XT / Radeon AI PRO R9700 (64 CU)', so 64 is the R9700 value (an earlier draft used 56, the RX 9070 non-XT figure — corrected). Chip profiles are PER-DEVICE: this row describes the R9700 specifically; a different gfx1201 SKU (e.g. the 16GB RX 9070 XT) gets its own row and verify_live correctly fails on VRAM/peak_bw mismatch. peak_bw_gbps=611.8 is MEASURED (warm DtoD-copy via peak_bw_probe, hipx R9700, force-high mclk=1258): the achieved DRAM copy peak. The prior committed 800.0 was an INCORRECT spec placeholder (bench_gemv_hfp4g32_bw::PEAK_GBPS) — the R9700 is 256-bit GDDR6@20Gbps = ~640 theoretical, and 611.8 is ~96% achieved. This re-grounds the roofline denominator (A3B decode %-of-roofline was overstated-low against the wrong 800). Cross-arch measured WARM peak_bw (GB/s): gfx1100=824 (~86% of 960), gfx1151=950 (SUSPECT: Strix APU ~256 LPDDR5X — the probe's l2+infinity_cache cache-clearing threshold from arch_spec is wrong for unified-memory APUs, so the copy hit cache; probe TODO), gfx1201=611.8, gfx1010=384 (~86% of 448), gfx1030=498 (~86% of 576). mem_latency_ns=205.888 is MEASURED **WARM** on the hiptrx **native-PCIe** R9700 (the campaign box; gfx1201, 2026-07-02) via pointer_chase_latency: 128 MiB single-thread dependent-load chase, elapsed/hops, at power_dpm_force_performance_level=high (mclk locked to state 5 = 1258 MHz, the sustained-inference DPM state). CORROBORATED by the hipx **TBT5-eGPU** R9700 warm = 206.9 ns (within 0.5%): the external dock adds nothing to on-device DRAM latency (the pointer-chase never touches the host<->device link). COLD is box-dependent noise (R9700 cold: hiptrx 470.8 / hipx-eGPU 548.8 / k9lin-9070XT 468.5 ns — different idle mclk states) but WARM converges to ~206 ns and is reproducible — cold-first profiling violates the DPM-warmup perf rule. Caveat: the microbench's reported sclk is a 2100 MHz placeholder so mem_latency_cycles is unreliable; the ns is the real measurement. Unblocks the latency/Little's-Law roofline. Cross-arch WARM sweep (hipx force-high) vs cold: gfx1010=274.2/769.7 gfx1030=146.8(IC-deflated)/152.1 gfx1100=169.7/310.1 gfx1151=220.0/220.0(iGPU no-sleep) gfx1201(R9700)=206.9/548.8 ns.
